request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the vozzik. A massive, barely-moving slug that grazes across the open dayside at a fraction of walking pace. Wherever it has gone, it has been going for a very long time; wherever it stops, it is likely to still be there years later. Visible features: an enormous slug body, far beyond any Earth slug; a broad rounded mantle dome; a wide grazing foot skirt; weathered, sun-baked brown and ochre hide; a low neck carrying the head and eye stalks close to the ground. In the rear view, seen from behind, the creature shows the same massive body as the front view: the broad rounded mantle dome and the wide foot skirt along its base are as wide and as tall as in the front view and fill the same share of the frame. The head and neck stay low and forward, hidden behind the mantle, and only the tips of the eye stalks show just beyond the top of the hump. In the front view, eyes toward the viewer, and in the side view, the neck slopes down below the top of the mantle. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, with a clean dark brown outline. The creature is rendered on a flat, neutral mid-grey backdrop that shares no hue with the hide, so the silhouette separates cleanly. The cut-out has a clean transparent edge all the way round: the foot's lower outline, the left and right tips of the foot, and the underside of the head each end in a crisp one-pixel antialiased step, and every antialiased edge pixel is the body's own tan, brown and ochre hide colour, matching the adjacent skin. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent final background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. All three show the same low, wide, slumped golden-ochre heap of soft wrinkled leathery material. Its top edge is wavy and overhanging, the base is lobed and pooling, and there is a dark central dimple or trough on top. On the sides are puckered, radially creased round openings: three on south, three on east, two on north. The outline is a thin dark brown line, the same weight on every facing. There is no keyline on any facing, and no eyes, fins, tail, limbs or scales. South and north are close to symmetric. East is longer, with its top fold draped diagonally and the left end bulkier than the tapering right end. All three facings are about the same height.
observed.south.png: A slumped golden sac seen from the front at the game's oblique angle. The top rim is wavy and folded with a dark dimple in its centre, like a deflated ball pushed in. A row of three puckered crater-like openings sits under the overhanging fold, the middle one largest. The lower edge is lobed. The leathery texture is finely mottled, with soft painterly shading. Thin dark outline, clean alpha, no shadow under it.
observed.east.png: Side profile of the same golden bag. It is longer and lower, with a large fold of skin draped diagonally over the top, forming a trough. Three puckered openings run along the flank, smallest at the right end. The left end is taller and bulkier, the right end tapers into a rolled lip. Same palette, texture and thin outline as south. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The same slumped bag from behind. A ring-shaped wavy rim surrounds a dark central dimple on top. One large puckered opening sits left of centre and a small one at the right, with heavier lobed folds at the base. There is no face and no eyes. It differs from south in the number and placement of openings and in the lobes, so it is not a copy. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom (211 px per cell, shrunk to fit), the candidate is a small flat golden heap about 75×28 px on brown ground beside a vanilla human whose head is about 130 px wide. The bag is roughly half the width of the vanilla head sprite and much flatter. At normal play (32 px per cell), it is a tiny golden-orange smear about a dozen px wide beside the human and the rat, with low contrast against the brown ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the camera-facing side of a faceless, roughly radial sac: three crater-mouths in a row under the overhanging top fold, seen from the oblique game camera. It is not a profile, not the rear and not overhead.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the sac, with the ring rim and two puckered openings. There are no eyes and no face. The openings are body orifices spread around the sac, not a face.

Add a card measure or a check that flags any facing whose opaque area is under about 40% of another facing's, whatever the height spread.
